subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add a core anti-drift enforcement layer for artifact-gated status updates, escalation timers, and post-green idle handling, or keep this as narrower opt-in diagnostics/tool-loop protection plus concrete bug fixes?
rationale: The request changes runtime policy, state ownership, config/defaults, and operator escalation UX; current main has partial adjacent guards but no obvious single implementation owner or default behavior.

options.title: Design One Core Guard Contract
options.body: Define the durable progress state, evidence fields, escalation events, defaults, and compatibility plan before implementation.

options.title: Keep Narrow Guard Fixes
options.body: Use existing loop detection, stuck-session diagnostics, and liveness mechanisms for concrete reproduced failures without adding a broader orchestration layer.

options.title: Wait For Stronger Repro
options.body: Keep the issue in needs-info until a current-main trace proves the exact status-loop and post-green idle failure modes.

recommendation.title: Design One Core Guard Contract
recommendation.body: Define the durable progress state, evidence fields, escalation events, defaults, and compatibility plan before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined trail across current loop/run-state files and related product-contract review context.
